approach: Add `pub fn check_design_existing_code(reading: &Reading) -> Result<()>` in reading.rs after `check_code_survey`, and `step!(check_design_existing_code(reading));` in `refusing_check` right after `step!(check_code_survey(reading));` (line 3061). It applies only to readings with a capability, no question, and class_of_work "design". It reads only the reading and needs (a) an assumption starting `Existing code:` that names a `crates/` or `docs/` path that is not a Create deliverable, and (b) a criterion with the words `existing code section` followed within 12 words by reuse or extend, with no negator from 3 words before the phrase through that word. Each failure bails with its own text naming the `Existing code:` label and what to list. The doc comment is one paragraph with no blank `///` lines. Add a sixth READING_RULES line of at most 220 bytes printed, so a correct reading passes on the first read. Add unit tests in reading.rs, corpus cases and a declaration test in refusal_corpus.rs, and a CHANGELOG entry. No model call, repository search or data file. Revision: the only findings were on criterion 9, so only its demonstration changes, to give a seam and fails_without. Everything else is as in the previous plan.

decisions.choice: Read only the reading (deliverables, assumptions, criteria) and accept a `crates/` or `docs/` path that is not a Create deliverable.
decisions.reason: The reader has no repo-search step and the brief forbids one. Excluding created paths refuses the case where the only 'existing code' named is the file the job creates. check_reading_references already checks that named paths exist when repo_files is supplied.

rejected.option: Check each named path against repo_files inside the new check
rejected.why: check_reading_references already does this; it would add a second source of truth and a signature change.

rejected.option: Accept any path-like token or any root directory
rejected.why: The brief fixes crates/ and docs/; broader matching accepts tokens such as owner/repo.

decisions.choice: Match the criterion on the word sequence 'existing code section' followed by a reuse or extend word within 12 words, with a negator guard from 3 words before the phrase to that word.
decisions.reason: This refuses 'the existing code in section 3 is unchanged' and 'no survey needed' (acceptance criterion 2) and is the narrowest rule that does. The refusal text gives the exact phrase.

rejected.option: Match 'existing code' and 'section' anywhere in the criterion

rejected.why: 'no existing code section is needed, nothing to reuse or extend' would pass.

rejected.option: Negation scan of the whole criterion
rejected.why: It refuses 'an Existing code section that reuses X and does not rewrite Y'.

decisions.choice: Place the step directly after check_code_survey in refusing_check.
decisions.reason: It keeps survey-type checks together. check_code_survey ignores design readings, so the order hides no refusal and the reader's one retry sees the root cause.

rejected.option: Append at the end of refusing_check
rejected.why: An unrelated check could refuse first and hide the missing Existing code.

decisions.choice: Add a sixth READING_RULES line instead of lengthening CODE_SURVEY_GUIDE.
decisions.reason: READING_RULES is printed in every reader brief and the rule-line test needs one line per check. BudgetSet::Reader covers CONTRACT, READER_FRAME, defaults and catalog (lib.rs 279-283), so the reader token headroom is not used. The limits are 220 bytes per line and 2400 bytes for the section.

rejected.why: Its test pins the exact text, it is about code and tests readings, and the section limit is shared.

decisions.choice: Add the corpus input form `design-existing-code`, four cases and a declared-intended test. INPUT_FORMS becomes 16 elements.
decisions.reason: Acceptance criterion 5 needs the case, the intended declaration and the every-step guard. A distinct tag makes corpus_covers_the_listed_input_forms fail if the case is lost.

rejected.why: Losing the case would go unnoticed.

decisions.choice: Demonstrate criterion 9 with the three Athena commands run at the repository root. Their seam is the workspace toolchain over the real tests, so no double or new fixture is needed.
decisions.reason: The criterion is the combined gate. It fails if any new code, test, rule line or changelog text breaks formatting, lints or an existing guard.

rejected.option: Run only the athena-core and athena-context tests
rejected.why: It misses fmt, clippy, the athena-cli budget tests and the xtask policy scan.

files.purpose: Add `pub fn check_design_existing_code(` with a one-paragraph doc comment and the path and criterion helpers after `check_code_survey`. Add the step line in `refusing_check`. Add the design_reading helper and unit tests `design_existing_code_*`.
Add the `design-existing-code` input form (INPUT_FORMS length 16), four design cases, and the declared-intended test.

steps: Read check_code_survey (reading.rs line 3375), code_surveys (3293), the refusing_check step list (step line at 3061), the tests near 7747-7974 (accept at 7772, doc-comment test splitting on `pub fn check_code_survey` at 7958), the refusal_corpus cases, INPUT_FORMS (line 70) and the guard at line 660, and READING_RULES (briefs.rs 1694) with its tests (3389-3417).

In reading.rs add helpers next to `code_surveys`. `existing_code_assumptions(reading) -> Vec<&str>` returns trimmed assumptions with the label `existing code:` in any case. `names_existing_path(text, creates: &[&str]) -> bool` splits tokens on white space, `,;'"()[]` and backtick, trims a trailing `.` or `:`, and accepts a token starting `crates/` or `docs/` followed by a letter or digit that is not a create path. `requires_existing_code_section(text) -> bool` rewrites `n't` to ` not`, lowercases, splits on non-alphanumerics, finds the words existing, code, section in sequence, takes the first reuse or extend word (reuse, reuses, reused, reusing, extend, extends, extended, extending) within 12 words after, and rejects a negator (no, not, never, without, nothing, nor, cannot) from 3 words before the phrase through that word.

Add `pub fn check_design_existing_code(` after check_code_survey. Its doc comment is a single paragraph with no blank `///` lines. It names the root cause (no inventory of existing code before a design is accepted, so a design that rebuilds or contradicts what is there is accepted), jobs 20261026-043137-zc0v and 20261026-065046-0c1d, that it reads only the reading, and the sentence 'This check refuses more readings; the higher refusal rate is intended.' Skip unless capability is Some, question is None and class_of_work is "design". Bail when no qualifying assumption exists, naming the `Existing code:` label and saying to list the crates/ or docs/ files, functions and docs the design changes or reuses, not files the job creates. Bail when no criterion qualifies, saying to add a criterion that requires an 'Existing code section' that reuses or extends them. The comment must not contain the string `pub fn check_code_survey`.

In `refusing_check` add `step!(check_design_existing_code(reading));` right after the check_code_survey step. In reading.rs tests add `design_reading(assumptions, criteria, deliverables)` on `scoped_reading` with class "design", and tests prefixed `design_existing_code_` for: accept; opposite criteria; created-only path; missing assumption; label without a path; other classes; question and decline; Modify versus Create on the same path.

In briefs.rs change `READING_RULES: [&str; 5]` to `[&str; 6]` and insert after the code survey line a rule such as: Existing code: a design reading has an `Existing code:` assumption naming crates/ or docs/ paths it does not create, and a criterion for an existing code section that reuses or extends them (`check_design_existing_code`). The printed line, including the '- ' prefix, must be at most 220 bytes; count and shorten if needed. Add `check_design_existing_code` to the check-name list in the rule-line test, change 'five rule lines' to 'six', assert one line contains both `Existing code:` and `check_design_existing_code`, and confirm the section stays under 2400 bytes.

In refusal_corpus.rs add `design-existing-code` to INPUT_FORMS (length 16) and the four cases. Build each with `case()` from base_reading with the class changed to design, and check that no earlier step refuses. Add `design_existing_code_refusal_is_declared_intended`, using `athena_core::reading::replay_declaration`, READING_SOURCE, and the changelog through `include_str!("../../../CHANGELOG.md")` with whitespace folding as the existing reading.rs test does.

Add the CHANGELOG.md entry under `## [Unreleased]` in the existing style: root cause, both jobs, the check and rule line, and the intended refusal with 'expected 5% of newly refused readings'. Write no email-like text and no banned words.

Run `cargo fmt --all`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --locked` and `cargo test -p athena-core --test refusal_corpus`. Confirm with `git diff --stat` that only the four deliverables changed.

risks.risk: The new rule line exceeds 220 bytes, or the section exceeds 2400 bytes.
risks.mitigation: Step 5 counts bytes before finishing. The existing test checks both limits. The estimate is about 2250 bytes of 2400, which I did not measure.

risks.risk: A legitimate design is refused because it touches only another root (xtask/, athena.toml), or because its criterion wording differs from 'existing code section'.
risks.mitigation: The refusal text names the exact phrase and the path roots, and the reader gets one retry with the refusal as a correction. The rule line teaches both. The path roots are the brief's choice.

risks.risk: The negator window refuses a good criterion, for example 'does not rewrite' between the phrase and 'reuses'.
risks.mitigation: The window runs only from 3 words before the phrase to the first reuse or extend word. Tests pin accepted forms, and the refusal text gives a sentence that passes.

risks.risk: A new corpus case is refused by an earlier step, so the guard looks satisfied for the wrong check.
risks.mitigation: Cases start from base_reading, which passes every step, and change only class, assumptions or criteria. Each asserts the exact step name.

risks.risk: The existing doc-comment test, which splits on `pub fn check_code_survey`, breaks.
risks.mitigation: The new function goes after check_code_survey and its comment avoids that string.

risks.risk: A reader still names only a created path.
risks.mitigation: The check filters created paths, the refusal says so, and the rule line says 'it does not create'.

risks.risk: The criterion 9 gate fails late on a policy scan (banned word or email-like text) in new text.
risks.mitigation: Step 7 forbids both. Running the full `cargo test --locked` in step 8 runs the xtask policy scan.

demonstrations.method: Unit tests in reading.rs `mod tests`. A new `design_reading(assumptions, criteria, deliverables)` helper is built on `scoped_reading` (line 5716) with class set to design. The accepting test goes through `accept` (line 7772, calls check_reading_acceptance, no repo_files). It uses assumption `Existing code: crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs and docs/design/jev-code-health.md`, a Create deliverable at another path, and criterion 'The design has an Existing code section that reuses or extends check_code_survey'. Variants use 'extends', 'reuses' and a lower-case label.
demonstrations.observes: Ok(()) from the real gate for each compliant design reading. A paired assertion in the same test calls `refusing_check` on the same reading with the assumption removed and expects the step name `check_design_existing_code`.
demonstrations.fails_without: The accepted-versus-refused pair fails: the step name is absent from refusing_check without the change, and the test does not compile without the new function.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry points `check_reading_acceptance` and `refusing_check` (exist). Fixtures `scoped_reading` and `accept` exist. The `design_reading` helper is added in plan step 4. No double.

demonstrations.method: Unit test through `accept` with a design reading that has a valid `Existing code:` assumption. Criteria are tried one at a time: 'no survey needed'; 'the existing code in section 3 is unchanged'; 'no existing code section is needed, nothing to reuse or extend'; 'existing code section' with no reuse or extend word; a reuse word more than 12 words after the phrase.
demonstrations.observes: Each returns Err whose text contains `Existing code` and the phrase 'existing code section'.
demonstrations.fails_without: A check matching 'existing code' and 'section' anywhere would accept the first two. A check with no negator guard would accept the third. Without the check all five are accepted.
demonstrations.seam: `check_reading_acceptance` via `accept` (exists). The `design_reading` helper is added in step 4. The criterion strings are the fixture; no double.

demonstrations.method: Unit tests through `accept`. (a) A Create deliverable at docs/design/new.md with the only assumption `Existing code: docs/design/new.md`. (b) No `Existing code:` assumption, with a `Code survey:` assumption naming crates/ present to show it does not count. (c) `Existing code: the reading module` with no path. Each has a valid criterion. A fourth test uses a Modify deliverable on the same path as (a) and expects acceptance.
demonstrations.observes: Err for (a), (b) and (c), with text naming the `Existing code:` label and saying to list existing paths the job does not create. The Modify case is Ok.

open_questions: Should paths in roots other than crates/ and docs/ (xtask/, athena.toml) count as existing code? The brief fixes crates/ and docs/, so the plan follows it. A later change could widen the roots.
The 5% share is the brief's estimate. No replay was run because records/ is absent, so it is unmeasured. The replay at verification gives the measured share.
